title: GraphPipe: Improving Performance and Scalability of DNN Training with Graph Pipeline Parallelism
problem: Existing pipeline-parallel DNN training systems partition models into sequential stages, ignoring the actual DAG topology of modern neural networks, which causes missed model-parallelism opportunities and suboptimal device utilization.
motivation: DNN models are growing beyond the capacity of a single GPU, and while pipeline parallelism is widely used, restricting pipeline stages to linear chains fails to exploit the branching and merging structure of modern architectures (e.g., transformers with parallel FFN+attention, multi-branch networks), leaving significant throughput on the table.
method: GraphPipe represents a neural network as a network of interconnected operations (a DAG, or directed acyclic graph) rather than a simple sequence. It identifies which operations can run in parallel and assigns them to separate processing devices (like GPUs). A scheduling algorithm then decides when to feed batches of data through these parallel stages, timing everything so devices stay busy without idle gaps.
key_novelty: Instead of forcing neural network computations into a sequential pipeline, it exploits the branching structure of the computation graph to run parallel sections on different devices simultaneously.
contributions: Formulation of graph pipeline parallelism that extends pipeline parallelism to arbitrary DNN DAG topologies.
Graph-aware partitioning and scheduling algorithm to minimize pipeline bubbles across non-linear stages.
GraphPipe system implementation for large-scale DNN training.
Demonstrated scalability and throughput improvements over sequential pipeline-parallel systems.

metrics.other: Throughput improvements over sequential pipeline baselines (details in full paper)

limitations: Graph partitioning complexity may limit scalability to very large numbers of devices with complex DNN DAGs; not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: graph-topology-aware pipeline parallelism for DNN training
